data.gender_notes: Gabian is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Gabian is derived from the Hebrew name Gabha meaning 'mountain' or 'hill'. In the Bible, the name Gabian is borne by a Hivite warrior who surrendered to Joshua and became an ally to the Israelites (Joshua 11:21). In the context of this biblical story, Gabian's name may reflect his strength and resilience, as he was a fierce warrior. In Christian tradition, the name Gabian is a reminder of God's strength and protection, evoking images of a mighty fortress or a steadfast rock. Gabian can be a meaningful choice for parents seeking to impart a sense of faith, courage, and loyalty to their child.
data.spiritual_meaning: A reflection of God's strength and protection for the child.
data.etymology: Gabian belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God is my strong one.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Gabian total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

Gabinus is said to have been buried in the crypt of the Saint-Sardos Basilica. The name 'Gabinus' may be derived from the Latin word 'gabinum', meaning 'hilly' or 'mountainous'.

Another tradition associates Saint Gauibald (also known as Gabian or Gabinius) with the monastery of Bobbio in Italy. According to legend, Gauibald was a hermit who lived in the sixth century AD and was visited by Saint Columban. Impressed by the hermit's piety, Columban established a monastery at Bobbio, which Gauibald became the abbot.
